ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In the circuit shown in figure, the open-circuit voltage of the power supply is 20V, the short-circuit current is 5A, and the load current \( I \) is 2A. What is the load resistance \( R \)?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is power source E, and below the power source an internal resistance R0 is connected in series; on the right side is load resistance R, and beside it the load current I is marked as flowing downward through R; the two ends of the circuit are marked with terminal voltage U, indicating the load terminal voltage. Reasoning: According to the data given in the problem, the power source open-circuit voltage Uoc = 20 V, short-circuit current Isc = 5 A, and load current I = 2 A. By the Thevenin equivalent relationship, internal resistance R0 = Uoc / Isc = 20 / 5 = 4 Ω. When the load current is 2 A, the voltage drop on the internal resistance is I R0 = 2 × 4 = 8 V. Therefore the load terminal voltage U = 20 - 8 = 12 V. Load resistance R = U / I = 12 / 2 = 6 Ω.

raw_record.question_text: In the circuit shown in figure, the open-circuit voltage of the power supply is 20V, the short-circuit current is 5A, and the load current \( I \) is 2A. What is the load resistance \( R \)?

method.method_draft: From the image identify R0 as the source's series internal resistance and R as the load carrying current I. From the text use Uoc = 20 V, Isc = 5 A, and I = 2 A. Compute R0 = 20/5 = 4 ohms. Then the internal voltage drop at 2 A is 2*4 = 8 V, so the load terminal voltage is U = 20 - 8 = 12 V. Finally R = U/I = 12/2 = 6 ohms.

method.method_draft: First describe the figure as an ideal voltage source E with internal resistance R0 feeding a series load R. From the text set E = Uoc = 20 V and Isc = 5 A, giving R0 = 20/5 = 4 ohms. For the actual load current I = 2 A, the total circuit resistance needed is E/I = 20/2 = 10 ohms.
